messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> PROD · router.latency.95th > 800ms (region: us-west) · severity: P3 · incident_id: PD12345
incident-bot: runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/incidents/router-latency · metric: router.latency.95th (1m) = 842ms · links: https://grafana/redwood/d/routers
maya: ack @here :hand: I'm on it, grabbing metrics and traces
liam: acked, oncall switching in 2m if I need to take over
maya: quick check — no error-rate spike in prod, just latency. synthetic-canary shows a sharp spike ~30s ago for us-west
liam: saw that too. single host/instance looks noisy: router-uw2-54. tracing shows long queue waits on kv-client
sre-oncall: canary-run id: synthetic/us-west/2026-03-17T12:34Z — it correlates w/ a CI job hitting internal endpoints?
ops-lead: any customer reports? support dashboard shows no increase in 5xx; CS pinged but no escalations
maya: running a quick DB of pods: `kubectl top pods -n routers | grep router-uw2-54` -> CPU 18% MEM 62% — not OOM. Network IO a bit higher
liam: grabbing tcpdump on that host, may be transient network hiccup with upstreams
incident-bot: PagerDuty: duplicate pages suppressed (auto-silence) · duplicates=3 · window=60s
maya: PD auto-silenced duplicates, looks like threshold tuning helped avoid noise, but initial page still fired
liam: pushed a temporary BGP route remove for router-uw2-54 to drain it from ELB, adding `kubectl cordon router-uw2-54` and `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets`
ops-lead: good call, keep an eye for any client reconnect churn
sre-oncall: post-drain 95th dropped to ~180ms within 40s — looks like that instance was the source
maya: incident-bot shows alert auto-resolve at 8055551388 · reason: metric returned below threshold for 3 consecutive windows
liam: re-enabled routing after 3 scale cycles, node looks healthy. running a synthetic resend: PASS
ops-lead: no customer impact confirmed, will mark as non-impacting. Notifying CS to close ticket if none come in 30m
maya: note to tune synthetic-canary weight and PD duplicate suppression window, the canary should be less likely to trigger primary alert path
liam: leaving handover note — I'm taking oncall for next 30m while maya heads to a meeting. ping me if it flaps again
maya: thanks, leaving details on the runbook snippet and query used:
```
SELECT percentile(latency, 95) FROM router_metrics
WHERE region = 'us-west' AND timestamp > now() - 5m
```
maya: adding retrospective action: add alert annotation when canary origin = synthetic and route to quieter channel / internal-only for 1st-fire
ops-lead: agreed. ops ticket created: OPS-4123 Tune canary routing + PD suppression.
incident-bot: thread auto-archived by incident-bot (no further activity for 20m)
liam: closing thread from oncall perspective — resolved, follow-up in OPS-4123 :white_check_mark:
